title: Flyto2 Core workflow engine -- T1552 ${env.VAR} interpolation reads any host secret the env.get denylist was meant to block
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-67427 (GHSA-hr7p-wg7r-hg9m,
CVSS 8.6 HIGH), affecting Flyto2 Core (`flyto-core`)'s workflow
engine.

Flyto2's capability policy denies the `env.get` and
`env.load_dotenv` modules by default, stating inline that they read
arbitrary host environment variables and are a secret-exfiltration
risk. But `VariableResolver` in
`src/core/engine/variable_resolver.py` expands `${env.VAR}` template
syntax for ANY environment variable, with no allowlist and no policy
check -- the interpolation happens earlier in the engine than
`enforce_module_policy`, so it is never subject to the module
denylist at all. A workflow parameter containing
`${env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}` resolves to the operator's live
secret in plaintext, and interpolating it into an outbound request
handled by any allowed module (the SSRF guard permits public hosts)
exfiltrates it to an attacker's server -- reachable via the workflow
API and the MCP agent surface, meaning the caller supplying the
template string is an LLM processing untrusted content, not the
trusted operator.

Detection logic flags a workflow step parameter containing the
`${env.` interpolation syntax -- the exact denylist-bypassing
template form this advisory's reproduction confirms resolves live
secrets even while the equivalent `env.get` module call is denied.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (flyto-core, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact resolver source file, a standalone
reproduction script, and confirmation through the running workflow
API), fixed in flyto-core 2.26.7+ (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
